newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB welcomes official restructure model.
newsitem.headline: AWB welcomes official restructure model.

text.p: The Australian government's Thursday announcement of the restructuring of the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) was the best and most positive news received for some time, AWB chairman Trevor Flugge said on Friday.

"The Australian wheat industry is leading the field in marketing wheat around the world but with the addition of this type of structure which gives grower ownership and control, coupled with single desk selling, we will be so far ahead of our competitors that they'll never catch us," he said in a statement.
The structure announced by the Primary Industries Minister John Anderson bridged the marketplace, government and grower groups, Flugge said.
He said Anderson's announcement showed an outline. "AWB is a big and complex company and there's an enormous amount of detail to be developed," he said.

"I am pleased to see that the single desk has been enshrined in legislation. It gives a strong and meaningful basis to operate and shows the commitment of the government to the industry," Flugge said.
He was commenting on Anderson's announcement on Thursday that the AWB was to become a private grower-owned company under a major corporate restructuring of the statutory body.
Class A shares are to be issued to wheat growers and B class shares to equity holders in the grower-funded Wheat Industry Fund.
The privatised AWB's export monopoly of Australian wheat would be retained under law, Anderson said.
